state:
Goal `core-metrics-and-4-more`, stage 2, per-member feature proofs. `Core\Metrics` and `Core\Mime`
are done and their group checks pass. `Core\Net::connect`, `listen` and `bindDatagram` carry every
proof, and `Core\Net\Datagram::send` does too. One Rust test and one `.nvst` case now carry
`covers:` markers for all eight datagram members, so no datagram member owes a test any more.
The members still owed are `Datagram::receive`, `port` and `close`, the three `Message` members,
and `Core\Net::connectLocal` and `listenLocal`. The two local members have a platform problem,
which item 3 below describes. Nothing is blocked.

next.title: the dossier
next.note: one file set: `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/net.rs`, and the `core/Net-Datagram/` and `core/Net-Datagram-Message/` directories under `docs/examples/`, `tests/hostile/` and `benches/members/`. Copy the `nvs.toml` from `docs/examples/core/Net-Datagram/send/`, `tests/hostile/core/Net-Datagram/send/` and `benches/members/core/Net-Datagram/`. That last one is already shared by the class.

items.text: **`Core\Net\Datagram::receive`, `port` and `close`** — about, 3 examples, hostile and bench each (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`). Tests are already credited. The class is at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/net.rs:701`, receive at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/net.rs:1806` and close at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/net.rs:1864`. `docs/examples/core/Net-Datagram/send/` is the model. A catch variable cannot be reused at a different exception type in one file, so name them `$io`, `$late` and `$e`.

**`Core\Net\Datagram\Message::payload`, `host` and `port`** — the same proofs. The class is at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/net.rs:886` and payload at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/net.rs:1880`. Its path is `core/Net-Datagram-Message/<member>`, and a `Message` exists only from a `receive`, so every proof binds two sockets first.

**`Core\Net::connectLocal` and `listenLocal`** — every proof except help, plus a Rust `covers:` marker on the path-grant test near `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/net.rs:2292`. The members are at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/net.rs:1422` and `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/net.rs:1452`. **This build has no Unix-domain transport on Windows** (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/net.rs:1491`), so a working example prints something different on Windows than on Linux. Only a grant refusal prints the same on both, because the grant is checked before the transport. The proof runner has no platform directive, only `requires: unimplemented` (`tools/nv/proofs/run.ts:54`). Recommended: add a `// requires: unix` directive beside it (skip on Windows, at `tools/nv/proofs/run.ts:165` and `tools/nv/proofs/run.ts:227`), document it in the three proof READMEs, and bless under WSL. Then decide how the Windows perf gate treats a bench it skips. The hostile case can be all grant refusals and pass on both.

backlog: `Core\Net\Datagram::send`'s recorded wall-clock is `0.0 ns/op` while its counts look right. Check how `nv proofs --record-perf` calibrates before trusting that column (`benches/members/README.md`).
